newsitem.title: USA: Arthuis - 2.3 pct 97 growth forecast a minimum.
newsitem.headline: Arthuis - 2.3 pct 97 growth forecast a minimum.

text.p: French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis repeated Monday he considered the government's forecast of 2.3 percent growth this year to be a minimum.

"All in all, the growth trend should reach 2.5 percent around the first half of this year and three percent at year-end," he said in a speech at the semi-annual meeting of the International Monetary Fund and World Bank.

"That notwithstanding, I have maintained a growth forecast of 2.3 percent on average for 1997 and 2.8 percent in 1998. These forecasts are deliberately conservative, I consider them to be a minimum," he said, according to a text of his speech.
He said France would continue to curb public expenditure.

"France is determined to continue this policy and deepen the structural reforms already undertaken to create new margins of growth for its economy in the medium term and thereby improve the labour market situation," he said.
It would also press ahead with reforms to the welfare system. "The increase in social spending will stay contained and the imbalances in social benefit financing eliminated," he said.
"Lastly, real labour market reform is another clear priority," he said.
